title.narrative: Strengthening Peacebuilding and Expanding Livelihood Opportunities for Rural Women in Benue State

description.narrative: Currently. the peace and security environment across Nigeria is characterized by multifaceted violent conflicts and threats to human security. Some of the threats include increased terrorist and violent extremist insurgency activities, transnational organized crimes, disasters as a consequence of climate change and environmental degradation impacts, and other human-induced factors. Factors such as ethnic politics, resource scarcity, population explosion, and urbanization have been identified as causes and accelerators of violence in Nigeria. Violent conflicts between farmers and herders in Nigeria so escalated and spiraled in recent years threatening the country’s security, stability and peace, and was ranked “as potentially dangerous as the Boko Haram insurgency in the Northeast. In spite of gross underreporting, in Benue State alone, between 2013 – 2016, official reports estimated that 1,878 persons were killed, 222 disappeared and 750 persons were grievously wounded. This number included 526 women, 200 (38%) of whom were pregnant, and another 231 (44%) nursing mothers. As of today (2022), only 2 (Gboko and Ushongo) out of the 23 LGAs have not been affected by the crisis. Benue state currently plays host to 27 IDP camps and about 2 million IDPs. (SEMA Report, 2022) The African Centre for Strategic Studies estimates that over 60,000 people have been killed in the violence across the Middle-Best region over the past 17 years (2001 to date), representing a yearly average of more than 3,500 people. In response to the prevalent humanitarian crisis outlined above, JDCF is proposing to undertake an intervention that will provide livelihood support to 200 victims of violent conflicts (vulnerable households) across 4 LGAs of Ado, Agatu, Oju, and Okpokwu. The funds will be channeled through Caritas Nigeria. However, the implementation will be done by JDPC Otukpo. CAFOD will work with Caritas to monitor and accompany JDPC throughout the project
